newsitem.title: UK: EMERGING EUROPE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST -AUG 12.
newsitem.headline: EMERGING EUROPE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST -AUG 12.

text.p: REUTERS EMERGING EUROPE PRESS DIGEST FOR ADVERTISING & MEDIA
Weekly Press Digest from Central and Eastern Europe on Advertising, Marketing, the Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
-- Russia's Novaya Reklamnaya Kompaniya advertising agency wins account to promote the new AvtoVAZ vehicle - VAZ-2110. (Kommersant-Daily, August 7, 1997)

-- Hungary will allow over-the-counter drugs to be advertised under a soon-to-be-issued decree by the Welfare Ministry. Advertising of prescription drugs will continue to be limited to events organised for the medical profession. (Vilaggazdasag, August 6, 1997)

-- Bulgarian National Television is to introduce new terms for commercials in September in a move to stabilise its finances, its new marketing director Petar Korumbashev says. (Capital, Aug 4-10, 1997)

-- A bill on the new Russian tax code would dispose of all limits on company advertising expenditures, a member of the State Duma budget committee says. Current regulations limit advertising expenditure to a certain percentage of company revenues. (Sevodnya, August 5, 1997)

-- More than 200,000 people work in Poland's direct marketing sector, with half working on a part-time basis, the Polish Direct Marketing Association says. (Dziennik Prawa i Gospodarki, August 1, 1997.)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

-- Central European Media Enterprises, the U.S.-based company whose Irisz TV recently lost bids to operate either of Hungary's two new commercial television stations, may launch a satellite broadcast in Hungary. CME has contacted Eutelsat, the satellite company, which could lead to "concrete talks and hopefully an agreement" in the future, Eutelsat spokeswoman Vanessa O'Connor said. (Vilaggazdasag, August 6, 1997)

-- The 1997 net profit of Poland's privately-owned Polsat television broadcaster will exceed the profits of state-owned Telewizja Polska (TVP) by at least 60 million zlotys ($17.3 million), says Piotr Fajs, president of PAI Media advertising agency. (Zycie, August 5, 1997)

-- Sofia Mayor Stefan Sofianski, following a visit to New York, says he and U.S. financier George Soros discussed the possibility of Sofia and the local branch of Soros's Open Society Foundation acquiring a joint stake in Bulgaria's private New Television. (Capital, Aug 4-10, 1997)

-- The Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung Group, owner of Bulgaria's mass-circulation 24 Chasa newspaper, has sacked its editor-in-chief Petyo Blaskov and is expected to replace him with his predecessor, Valeri Naidenov. (Sega, Aug 7-13, 1997)

-- The co-owner and former chief executive of the Czech Republic's Radio City, Petr Dvorak, asks the Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting to cancel Radio City's licence because the station failed to reach an agreement with RTL. (Strategie News, July 9-16, 1997)

-- National broadcasting firm Antenna Hungaria (AH) Rt seeks a determining role in the Hungarian telecommunications market, with plans to enter the 1800 Mhz mobile telephone market and a desire to strengthen its position in satellite, microwave and cable telecommunications. (Vilaggazdasag, August 4, 1997)

-- Bulgaria's cash-strapped National Radio is to cut its staff by 10 percent and take some regional programmes off the air in a move to overcome its financial crisis, its new director Lilyana Popova says. (Capital, Aug 4-10, 1997)
-- Ringier CR will invest into the Czech daily newspaper Lidove Noviny. (Strategie News, July 9-16, 1997)

-- Poland's Wolne Slowo publishing, which owns the conservative Zycie daily newspaper, will sell up to 49 percent of the group to a Warsaw-based company, Wolne Slowo board member Wojciech Mikulecki said. (Gazeta Wyborcza, August 7, 1997)

-- Bulgaria's Constitutional Court is expected to rule in the second half of September on an appeal by the main opposition Socialist Party to declare void the replacement of state media heads voted by the parliament in mid-July.
(Capital, Aug 4-10, 1997)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS/MARKETS & CONSUMER TRENDS:

-- Hungary's tourism revenues in 1997 are expected to reach an earlier stated annual target of 2.43 billion forint ($12.2 million). Income from tourism recorded to date totals 739 million forints, 30 percent more than in the year-ago period. In the first half of 1997 1.3 billion forints was spent on tourism, including marketing expenses of 835 million forints. (Vilaggazdasag, August 6, 1997)

-- U.S.-based United Cinemas International will build 10 large-screen cinemas around Poland in the next three years worth $100 million, deputy president Ray Smith says. (Gazeta Wyborcza, August 1, 1997)

-- The 12th Hungarian Formula 1 Marlboro race may produce 10 billion forints in indirect revenues, with income from tourism contributing up to five to seven billion forints, says Janos Berenyi, head of race organiser Hungaroring Sport Rt. Ticket revenues are expected to be about 1.1 billion to 1.2 billion forints, and the race may break even this year. (Vilaggazdasag, August 6, 1997)

-- A consortium led by Bank Handlowy will buy a 75-percent stake in the Domy Towarowe Centrum, Poland's largest department store chain, following approval by the treasury ministry, the bank says. (Rzeczpospolita, August 7, 1997)
CONSUMER TRENDS:

-- Half of Poland's GSM mobile telephone subscribers are independent businesspeople, and 20 percent of subscribers are women, according to a report by Era GSM operator. It says the average age of mobile users is falling. (Gazeta Wyborcza, August 4, 1997)
